capabilities: Rewrite only the property that changed, keeping comments, quotes, blank lines, indentation and inline lists
Skip writes when a property change alters nothing
Patch processFrontMatter() and enable formatting-preserving mode in obsidian-lib-based plugins
Fall back to Obsidian's own rewrite when a change cannot be spliced in faithfully
Ship a demo vault comparing behavior with the plugin on and off
disambiguation: Not a YAML formatter or linter; it only stops Obsidian from reformatting frontmatter lines a change does not touch.
extras: No settings: installing is the switch and disabling restores Obsidian's default behavior. Beta versions install via BRAT. A demo vault ships with every release and doubles as the documentation; another plugin that patched processFrontMatter() before this one loads will not be called for Markdown files.
intentEvidence: It covers every plugin that edits front matter through app.fileManager.processFrontMatter(), which includes some of Obsidian's own edits
problem: When any plugin edits a property, Obsidian rewrites the entire frontmatter block, destroying comments, quotes, blank lines and inline list style even in untouched properties.

relations.evidence: Same preservation goal; also preserves inline comments, quotes, whitespace and lists; covers obsidian-lib writes

summary: Frontmatter protection patch that rewrites only the changed property so comments, quotes, blank lines and inline lists survive plugin edits.
